office_does: One of 49 Washington State Senators, serving four-year terms writing state law and the state budget for the 37th District (southeast Seattle, Skyway and part of Renton).
race_blurb: Open seat between two Democrats: Rep. Chipalo Street, who voted for the millionaires' tax and rent stabilization and has broad labor and party backing, and first-time candidate Tatiana Brown, an environmental-justice organizer who refuses corporate and PAC money. Street took 73.8% in the primary.

candidates.summary: State Representative since 2023 and Microsoft technologist, running for the open Senate seat with endorsements from the outgoing senator, the House Speaker, labor unions and the King County Democrats.
highlights: Voted for the 2026 millionaires' tax and campaigns on it [S1][S6]
Voted for the 2025 rent-increase limit and cites zoning reform to increase home building [S1][S8]
Cites banning ICE agents from wearing masks and stopping Flock camera surveillance; supports barring ICE from courthouses [S1][S5]
Cites restoring abortion funding; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Advocates Washington and Pro-Choice Washington [S1][S4]

taxes.basis: Voted for and champions the millionaires' tax, calling it 'a one in one hundred year bill.'

spending.basis: Cites $131 million in district capital investments and says the millionaires' tax funds education and healthcare access.

housing.basis: Voted for the 2025 rent-increase limit and cites 'tenant protections like rent stabilization,' alongside zoning reform to increase home building.

safety.basis: Says 'investment in our communities is the only sustainable path to real public safety' and partners with police-accountability groups; also cites an assault weapons ban.

experience.basis: Sitting legislator since 2023 with an enacted record, but a short tenure compared with long-serving incumbents.

immigration.basis: Cites banning masked ICE agents and maintaining food assistance for immigrants; supports barring ICE from courthouses and a state CDL for immigrants.

social.basis: Cites restoring abortion funding and is endorsed by Planned Parenthood Advocates Washington and Pro-Choice Washington; no documented gender-identity position.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which narrowed I-2081's parental notification and records rights; no public statements on the topic.

reform.basis: Pamphlet statement runs on "unmatched endorsements from labor and environmental advocates"; site lists an extensive party, labor and officeholder coalition.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate, co-chair of the Washington Environmental Justice Council and collaborative-governance strategist, running on progressive revenue, climate justice and community assemblies without corporate or PAC money.
highlights: Rejects corporate, PAC, fossil-fuel and 'war profiteer' donations; small-donor funded [S3]
Wants government-funded community assemblies so 'the people most impacted by public policy should help create it' [S1]
Calls for a statewide moratorium on new hyperscale AI data centers and making data centers pay for their energy use [S4]
Would formally refuse ICE cooperation and champion SB 5906 to 'ICE-proof' schools [S4][S5]

taxes.basis: Wants the wealthiest to pay their fair share; proposes new progressive revenue, closing the data-center sales-tax exemption and a higher top real-estate excise tax bracket.

spending.basis: Pledges to direct investments into the district and fully fund school counselors and social workers, and to defend college grants.

climate.basis: Co-chairs the Environmental Justice Council implementing the HEAL Act, helped shape CCA advocacy, and runs on climate justice.

experience.basis: First run for elected office; community-organizer profile against a sitting legislator.

reform.basis: Refuses corporate and PAC money and campaigns on government-funded community assemblies.

immigration.basis: Would formally refuse ICE cooperation, decommission the Tacoma detention center and pass the SAFE Act to 'ICE-proof' schools.

tech.basis: Calls for a statewide moratorium on new hyperscale AI data centers and for developers to pay for their energy use.
